assessments.reasoning: The Index’s SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 admits historical editions. Its license criterion at bytes [533,942) applies to the edition-specific OSI text and its operative grants. The Wayback raw capture 20061001134907id_ preserves the OSI origin http://opensource.org/licenses/osl-2.0.txt. The 9,964-byte plaintext receipt matches the claimed revision. Its heading and prescribed notice at bytes [269,321) identify version 2.0. Sections 1–3 address copyright, patents and source code. The opening paragraph conditions application to an Original Work on its owner placing the specified notice.

OSI’s license-discuss archive preserves Lawrence Rosen’s signed 8 September 2021 reply and the quoted exchange, SHA-256 203753e50d9da13cd4e735867cbc305b07b25e251d62f17c4d84f7702636e245. Although the subject names AFL, Rosen expressly includes pre-3.0 OSL at bytes [5751,5874), calls those versions “no longer valid” and asks for removal. Smith proposes “superseded” for legacy uses. Rosen recalls prior board approval, while Brasseur reports that the SPDX team lacked definitive proof. This supports authorial chronology only. The correspondence supplies neither board minutes nor a ruling on existing grants.

The Index decision at afb962e68831a16accb80c70159b1e2f1fbb4dbc, bytes [5398,5591), records `758efdc08d9944d1b2ff803bcb9bd721`, Open Software License 2.0, `osl-2-0`, `sha256:f16caf37737d270c42c451ea92dd5591979f269a7cc130a6f809c6c8cc2f9d3b`, `license`, `historical`. The opaque ID matches the claim subject after its `e-` prefix. This row directly establishes the editorial value independently of any interpretation of Rosen’s request.

challenge.method: Compared the 2.0 plaintext and Index row with the adjacent 2.1 and 3.0 rows. Tested whether Rosen’s removal request established an Index deletion, a board decision or termination of existing grants.
challenge.results: OSL 2.1 also has `historical` but has a different entity and digest. OSL 3.0 has `active` and a different edition. The witness’s version notice selects 2.0. The Index expressly retains this row. The correspondence records the author’s view, a proposal for legacy uses and uncertainty about documentary proof of board approval. None conflicts with the scoped identity or the Index’s own retention decision.

limitations: The witness establishes historical publication at the OSI origin. Lawrence E. Rosen holds the copyright identified in the text. Present publisher currency and formal OSI board action have separate evidentiary scopes.

Rosen’s request to remove earlier versions and Smith’s proposal to retain them as superseded document different positions. The legal effect on existing grants and any SPDX deprecation decision remain undetermined by this evidence.

`historical` retains the reference for reconciliation and documentary lookup after selection. Work-specific use, redistribution, installation eligibility and consumer release authorization require separate evidence.
